mission: Hard universal process and script rules for NMS Base Builder Python generation.

rules.summary: Generated build geometry must be real NMS Base Builder plugin parts, not generic Blender primitives.
The complete object library must be inspected for part selection; short lists are examples only.
Before providing any script, run a validation loop against universal rules, the script ObjectID set, applicable part-family rules, issue/fix lessons, prohibited parts, and audit requirements.
rules.deviation_policy: If a rule must be violated because it is bad, stale, or constrains design intent, request approval before delivering code.

rules.summary: For placement validation, calibrated spacing/depth/orientation rules, issue/fix checks, and part-family lessons, review only ObjectIDs and part families that actually appear in the current script/build.
rules.design_exception: Broad library review remains appropriate for design potential and part selection.

rules.summary: When a design rule, offset correction, orientation fix, spacing formula, or part-specific behavior is understood and correctly applied, immediately update the master docs/rules/registries.
rules.purpose: Prevent durable lessons from living only in one chat or one script.

rules.summary: Object location is the Blender origin, not guaranteed visible center. Use FBX extents and centers to compute bottom/top placement.
Do not name or describe trim/wall rows as continuous unless parts actually touch or overlap from the viewer angle.
rules.fix: Compute centers from scaled visible length and deliberate overlap; add end/corner closures where needed.

rules.summary: Resolve NMS builder runtime before deleting or modifying scene objects. Never clear a scene before preflight succeeds.
HOLO_DISCO is Wonder Projector and should not be generated because it requires in-game configuration.
rules.allowed_exception: Only preserve an already configured user-provided object when explicitly requested.

rules.summary: U_PARAGON is plugin/default placeholder or non-visible artifact. Do not classify it as Wonder Projector or design around it as visible geometry.
Every substantial script/build must record ObjectID roles and use types in a BUILD OBJECT USE MANIFEST.
Creative/nonliteral part applications from screenshots, JSON, studies, or user feedback must be logged immediately.
Architecture and base screenshots must be mined for transferable build lessons.
Broad experimental/creative prompts activate exploration mode, not consolidation mode.
banned_patterns: ten variants of the same comfortable motif
weak variants kept only to fill count

rules.summary: Every part in an experimental build must have a visible architectural, mechanical, visual, or effect role.
banned_patterns: part added because it looks finished
subterrain part with no visible effect

rules.summary: Mode-specific repositories such as Corvette must be applied only when the prompt or ObjectID set activates that mode. Universal generator rules still apply, but mode-specific requirements must not leak into unrelated builds.
Corvette ObjectID presence alone does not activate Corvette build validation.
rules.rule: If Corvette parts are used decoratively/non-functionally in a non-Corvette build, validate them as normal ObjectIDs and record their use type; do not require seven Corvette categories.
activates_corvette_mode_when: user asks for Corvette/ship/Corvette module/Corvette Workshop output
script claims to create a valid Corvette
object-use manifest assigns Corvette functional roles

rules.summary: HOLO_DISCO_0 is also a Wonder Projector and should not be generated because it requires in-game configuration.
rules.allowed_exception: Only preserve an already configured user-provided object.

rules.summary: Use validated XnZY + RIGHT_AT_UP + POST_RX90 + LOCAL_Y_180 transform stack for the current exported NMS base JSON intake path.
rules.caveat: Audit and validate new/unseen ObjectID families before treating as universal across all NMS parts.

rules.summary: Use finished-base JSON as a placement dataset to extract ObjectID roles, scale, spacing, connections, module recipes, and negative lessons.
Stairs/ramps/vehicles/tabletop games/display walls/powerline hubs/rings must use endpoints, local frames, or ring logic rather than independent scatter.
Ignore/exclude powerlines, switches, batteries, solar panels, biofuel generators, and related utility devices by default unless explicitly requested.
Treat dome/cylinder/spire/hull examples as instances of broad connected-piece curvature grammar, not only exact named recipes.
Classify the prompt and apply triggered rules before acting; protocol-sensitive responses require a Protocol confirmation section.
